rules.title: Do not use `any`
rules.description: Do not write the TypeScript `any` type in the code: `: any`, `as any`, `any[]`, `Array<any>`, `<any>`. Only report places where the keyword `any` is written, and quote that code including the word `any`. Use a concrete type, a generic, or `unknown` instead.
rules.notAViolation: Code that only returns or passes along an implicit `any`, e.g. `JSON.parse(raw)` or `as User[]`. The word "any" inside a string or a comment, or as part of a name such as `anyValue` or `company`.

rules.title: No `console.log`
rules.description: Do not leave `console.log(...)` calls in committed code.

rules.title: Use `===` and `!==`
rules.description: Compare values with strict equality `===` and `!==`. Every loose comparison `==` or `!=` is a violation.

rules.title: No empty `catch`
rules.description: A `catch` block must handle the error: log it, show it to the user, or rethrow it. A violation is a `catch` block that is empty or contains only comments, e.g. `catch {}` or `catch (e) { }`.
rules.notAViolation: A `catch` block with any statement inside.
